# 0011. Shape of the code generated by `#[machine]`

Status: accepted
Date: 2026-11-12
Spec: 4, 5.3, 6.2, 6.3, 6.5; ADRs 0001, 0002, 0005-0010

## Context

M2 wrote scenarios A, B, D and I by hand against `estado-core`, as the macro would generate them (`examples/a_http_parser/`, `b_connection/`, `d_game_character/`, `i_media_player/`; core test machines in `crates/estado-core/tests/support/`). M3 makes the macro produce that code. This ADR fixes the shapes the generators follow, so that 4.2 (handler rewrite) and 4.3 (Spec impl) agree, and records the one change from the hand-written code: in-place writes for transitions below the root (BM-01, ADR 0009).

## Decision

### Placement and names

- Everything generated lives in `#[doc(hidden)] pub mod __estado` inside the machine module, except the public views and the state id consts, which are emitted in the machine module (ADR 0010).
- State ids: associated consts on the root type, `Player::PLAYING`, numbered in pre-order from 0 (graph index).
- Views (ADR 0007): `<Composite>Fields<'a>` with `&'a mut` to every shared field of a compound or parallel struct, with `reborrow(&mut self) -> <Composite>Fields<'_>`; `<Variant>Mut<'a>` for struct-like variants (tuple view for tuple variants); `<Variant>Exiting` owned struct when a constructor exits a struct-like variant or a compound with `#[history(deep, keep)]` (errata 5).
- Generated enums carry `#[allow(clippy::enum_variant_names)]`; every generated item gets a descriptive name, no hashes (spec 6.5).

### Handlers (4.2)

- The `#[handlers]` impl is re-emitted with each handler rewritten in place, keeping the user's body:
  - a generic `S: ::estado_core::Sink<Effect>` is added; `&mut Cx<Self>` becomes `&mut Cx<'_, Self, S>`;
  - the event parameter gets a named lifetime `'event`;
  - `-> Next<Self>` becomes `-> Next<Self, __estado::<Handler>Edges<..>>` when the handler has no constructor-form `goto!`, else `-> Next<Self, impl Edge<Self> + use<'event, S>>` (ADR 0001);
  - `-> Result<Next<Self>, E>` keeps the `Result` around the rewritten `Next` (spec 6.4).
- Parameters are recognised by type, in the order of spec 6.2: own data (`&mut T`, `TMut<'_>`, or nothing), ancestor `*Fields` (nearest first), `&mut Cx<Self>`, `&Event`. A compound's own handler receives its `*Fields`, never `&mut` to the whole struct (R3, ADR 0007).
- One edge enum per handler, one variant per `goto!` occurrence; simple-form variants carry the already-built value of the LCA child; constructor-form variants carry the closure, one generic parameter each.
- `stay!()`, `bubble!()`, `unhandled!()`, `defer!()`, `reenter!()` expand to the `Next` variants; `goto!` outside a handler is E0040.

### Transition code (4.3)

- Per state, generated `exit_<state>` and `enter_<state>` functions that exit the active descendants then the state (deepest first, regions in reverse declaration order), or enter the state then its active descendants (regions in declaration order), including spec 5.3 steps 2, 3, 8, 9: cancels, history recording, epochs, scheduling. Each edge's `apply` is linear code calling them: exit segment, take or write, constructor, entries.
- **In-place rule.** A simple-form edge writes the new value of the LCA child in place (`*children_field = value`, after the exits; the old value is dropped there). Only constructor-form edges take ownership: the slot is taken (`Slot::take`), destructured down to the LCA child, rebuilt around the constructor's result, and put back (ADR 0002). Transitions at the root level with the simple form also write in place through `Slot::live_mut`.
- `changed` is computed by comparing the active leaf ids before and after when the edge targets the handler's own state or an ancestor (ADR 0006); otherwise `true`.
- `#[inline(always)]` on `microstep` and on the per-composite dispatch functions; user handlers get `#[inline]` (spec 6.5). If BM-01 shows the forced inline is needed, errata entry per ADR 0009.

### Dispatch and runtime

- `microstep` is a nested `match` from the root to the leaf; a `Bubble` falls through to the parent's handler in the same frame; regions follow ADR 0005/0008 (sequential, short-circuit when an edge leaves the parallel state, `refresh_active` after a region-internal transition only when `TRACKS_ACTIVE`).
- `TRACKS_ACTIVE` is true only when some handler calls `cx.in_state`; it is detected syntactically.
- The `Runtime` struct holds only what is used: `Queues<Event, raise_cap, defer_cap>` when `cx.raise` or `defer!()` appears, else `NoRuntime`; one `u32` epoch per state with timers or invokes; shallow history as `Option<u8>`, deep history as `Option<SubstateEnum>`; one `bool` for pending `#[always]` or completion (ADR 0005). With nothing used it is `NoRuntime<Event>` (AC-15).
- `timer_event` and `accepts_invoke` match the active state and epoch; the timer event expression is evaluated on the current state data (spec 7.1).
- `GRAPH` is a `static` built from the tree and the edge enums (`TARGETS`, `event_hint`).

## Consequences

- The hand-written M2 scenarios are the reference: M3 rewrites them with the macro and both versions must pass the same tests (spec 12). Differences are limited to the in-place rule and naming.
- Generators can be written and tested independently against this contract: views, edges and handlers (4.2), runtime, entries/exits, dispatch and `Spec` (4.3).
